title: When the Vow Burns
premise: Gideon Eastwick, a widowed single parent who runs the only bookshop in the fading town of Marrow's Bend, has spent ten years keeping their heart under strict discipline—until their grandmother's will demands every Eastwick heir arrive at the family reunion with a partner or forfeit their inheritance of the shop's building. Desperate, Gideon asks Wren Calloway, the traveling bookbinder who repairs their damaged volumes, to pose as their date for one weekend. What begins as a transaction curdles into something terrifyingly genuine, forcing Gideon to confront the vow of self-containment made at their spouse's deathbed. When the will's true clause is revealed—grandmother intended to gift the building to whoever the shop's keeper truly loved—Gideon must speak the rehearsed sentence of grief and love aloud, choosing found family over safe invisibility, and the story ends with Wren staying, the bookshop reborn as a community home.
about_author: Quentin Fairweather is the pen name of a former rare-book cataloguer who spent a decade in auction houses before turning to fiction, and who claims to have fallen in love twice: once in a reading room, once in a bindery. Fairweather writes small-town romances about people who mistake caution for character, and lives quietly with a dog named Marginalia.

chapters.title: The Weight of Unread Letters
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Morning routine at Eastwick Books: opening the shop, school-run chaos with nine-year-old Juniper, and the arrival of a solicitor's letter from the Eastwick estate. Gideon reads it twice and files it under 'later.' The emotional beat is quiet dread—the first crack in a decade of careful order.

chapters.title: A Binder of Broken Things
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren Calloway sets up their traveling bindery in the bookshop's back room for the autumn season, repairing water-damaged stock. They observe Gideon's precise, armored kindness and find it fascinating. The beat is curiosity meeting caution; Wren recognizes a fellow keeper of fragile things.

chapters.title: Terms of the Will
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The solicitor, Ms. Okafor, explains the clause: each Eastwick heir must attend the reunion with a partner of at least one year's standing, or their claim to the shop building lapses. Without the building, the bookshop dies. Gideon refuses to beg the family. Beat: cornered pride.

chapters.title: Juniper's Wish List
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV (close third). Juniper, doing homework in the shop, overhears the will problem and privately lists reasons her parent should 'get a person.' She loves Wren's stories about cities. The beat is a child's innocent scheming, tender and funny, raising stakes without Gideon knowing.

chapters.title: An Offer, Badly Made
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Over closing-time tea, Gideon asks Wren—awkwardly, transactionally—to pose as their partner for the reunion weekend. Payment: the building's rare bindery, permanently theirs. Wren is insulted by the framing but intrigued by the shop. Beat: friction with an undertow of mutual attraction.

chapters.title: Counteroffer
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren agrees, but on their terms: no payment, and Gideon must teach them the town—its people, its stories—as if the courtship were real practice. Gideon accepts before examining why. Beat: the fake relationship begins with a handshake that lingers too long.

chapters.title: Rehearsal Dinner for Two
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. First 'date': learning each other's histories to survive interrogation. Wren asks questions no one has asked since the funeral. Gideon deflects with book trivia; Wren lets it pass, once. Beat: intimacy disguised as research, and the first involuntary honesty.

chapters.title: The Eastwick Gallery of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren studies the family: Aunt Verity the matriarch-in-waiting, cousins with rival claims, and the portrait of Grandmother Odile. Wren notices Gideon's name absent from the family wall. Beat: outsider's clarity—Gideon has been erased, and has agreed to it.

chapters.title: Ten Years of Small Silence
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Flashback woven through a sleepless night: the deathbed vow to Sam—'I'll keep everything safe, I'll keep myself contained'—and the decade of discipline since. Beat: the reader learns why Gideon equates love with loss; the vow is named for the first time.

chapters.title: Practice Kissing Is Not a Thing
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper demands the 'couple' practice for the reunion, staging a fake dinner in the shop. Gideon and Wren, playing along, accidentally have a real moment over candlelight and leftover cake. Beat: comedic warmth tipping into genuine want, witnessed by a delighted child.

chapters.title: Road to Hollowmere Hall
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The drive to the reunion estate, Juniper in the back seat, nerves climbing. Gideon briefs Wren on family landmines; Wren notices Gideon's hands shaking on the wheel. Beat: threshold crossing—leaving the safety of the shop and entering hostile, glittering territory.

chapters.title: Arrival, Performed
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. First hours at Hollowmere: introductions, appraisal, Verity's velvet hostility toward Gideon and open curiosity about Wren. Wren performs the devoted partner flawlessly and hates how easy it feels. Beat: the masquerade works too well.

chapters.title: Dessert and Detonation
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. At the welcome dinner, a cousin mocks Gideon's 'stranger partner,' and Wren answers with a story about Gideon that is invented and entirely true. Gideon, undone, realizes the fake date has become real by dessert. Beat: the blurb's pivot—the heart slips its training.

chapters.title: Corridor Confession
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren corners Gideon after dinner: 'That wasn't acting for me.' Gideon denies it, badly, and asks for rules. Wren refuses to pretend it isn't happening. Beat: first open conflict—desire versus denial, with Juniper asleep down the hall raising the stakes.

chapters.title: The Library Clause
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Gideon finds Odile's private library, unlocked for heirs, and a letter addressed to 'the keeper of the shop.' It hints the will has a second, hidden condition. Beat: mystery deepens; Odile posthumously meddles, and Gideon wonders if grandmother saw through everything.

chapters.title: Morning After, Carefully Ordinary
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Breakfast theater for the family: shared glances, a hand at Gideon's back that neither wants to withdraw. Verity probes Wren's roots and finds no Eastwick pedigree. Beat: Wren realizes they are falling for Gideon and for the idea of staying somewhere.

chapters.title: Juniper and the Rose Garden
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper, exploring the estate, meets great-aunt Odile's old gardener, who tells her Odile once loved a bookseller the family rejected. Juniper begins connecting dots. Beat: the past rhyming with the present through a child's ears; hope planted.

chapters.title: Rival Claims
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Cousin Marcus proposes buying Gideon out regardless of the will's outcome, offering escape money. Gideon is tempted by the clean exit—until they picture the shop empty. Beat: the temptation of invisibility made literal and financial.

chapters.title: Storm at Hollowmere
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A storm traps the reunion indoors; power fails; candles and ghost stories. Wren and Gideon end up alone in the conservatory, and the almost-kiss finally happens. Beat: the midpoint—desire wins one night, and both know the fiction has collapsed.

chapters.title: What We Agreed Not to Say
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Morning after: Gideon retreats into the vow, telling Wren the weekend must return to script. Wren, hurt, agrees coldly. Beat: the false low point—Gideon chooses containment and immediately regrets it; the reader feels the cost.

chapters.title: The Family Interrogation
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Verity privately interrogates Wren, revealing she knows the relationship began weeks ago and offering Wren money to walk away and discredit Gideon's claim. Beat: Wren's loyalty tested; they pocket nothing and say nothing—yet—protecting Gideon from the knowledge.

chapters.title: Letters in the Bindery
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Back home early, Gideon repairs a damaged Odile book and finds more letters sewn into the binding: Odile's own lost love, a bookseller, and her regret at choosing the family's approval. Beat: Gideon sees their own future in the grandmother's past and is shaken.

chapters.title: Juniper Asks the Question
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper asks Gideon directly if Wren is 'a real one or a pretend one,' and whether pretend ones leave. Gideon cannot lie to her. Beat: devastating clarity through a child's eyes; Gideon realizes the stakes were never the building.

chapters.title: The Sentence, Rehearsed
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Alone at closing time, Gideon speaks aloud the deathbed sentence never finished: 'I promise to keep everything safe—including my heart from—' and cannot end it. Wren, unseen in the bindery, hears. Beat: dramatic irony and aching proximity; the truth almost spoken.

chapters.title: Wren's Suitcase
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren begins packing, deciding it's kinder to leave before being asked. Juniper catches them and begs them to stay, revealing Gideon's sleeplessness and the half-spoken sentence. Beat: Wren chooses to stay and fight, not flee—found family asserted.

chapters.title: Verity's Ultimatum
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Verity arrives at the shop with the solicitor: she has evidence the relationship is fraudulent and will invoke a morality-and-fraud clause unless Gideon withdraws. Beat: the antagonist closes in; Gideon must decide whether to lie to save the shop or tell the truth and risk everything.

chapters.title: The Town Weighs In
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Word spreads; the town that Gideon quietly served for a decade shows up—regulars, teachers, Juniper's classmates' parents—filling the shop in silent support. Beat: Gideon, watching from the register, understands they were never invisible; they were loved all along.

chapters.title: Reading Odile's Last Letter
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. With Wren beside them, Gideon opens the final sewn letter: Odile's will's true intent—the building goes to 'the keeper of the shop and whoever they love enough to say it aloud,' with proof being the spoken vow, witnessed. Beat: the mechanism of the climax revealed; saying it is the test.

chapters.title: Refusal and Ruin
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. At the estate's final gathering, Verity demands Gideon publicly confess fraud or forfeit. Gideon, terrified of the vow, begins to withdraw the claim—choosing the old safety. Beat: the all-is-lost moment; Wren's face as Gideon lets go.

chapters.title: Juniper Stands Up
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper, in front of the whole family, reads aloud from Odile's letters that she found and kept, telling the room about Odile's bookseller and asking why love has to be a secret to count. Beat: the child becomes the catalyst; the room turns; Verity's certainty cracks.

chapters.title: The Gardener's Testimony
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Odile's old gardener arrives with the original letter Odile wrote to her bookseller, never sent, proving the will's intent and Verity's suppression of it. Okafor validates it. Beat: justice through the past; the legal threat collapses, but the emotional one remains—Gideon still hasn't spoken the vow.

chapters.title: Wren at the Door
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren tells Gideon they're leaving at week's end—not from anger, but because they won't stay where they're only half-chosen. They leave the finished repair of Sam's damaged first-edition gift on the counter. Beat: the ultimatum of self-respect; Gideon alone with the book and the choice.

chapters.title: Sam's Book, Gideon's Answer
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Gideon finally reads the inscription Sam left inside the repaired book: 'Keep everything safe—except your heart. Let it burn.' The deathbed vow, understood at last, was permission, not prohibition. Beat: the revelation that reframes ten years; grief and love reconciled.

chapters.title: The Sentence Spoken
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Gideon finds Wren at the train platform and speaks the rehearsed sentence, completed at last: the vow, the grief, and 'I choose you—not as practice, not as proof, as home.' Beat: the climax's emotional peak; the public, witnessed declaration Odile's letter required.

chapters.title: Witnessed
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The town, Juniper, even a grudging Verity witness the declaration at the shop; Okafor records it per the will's terms. Wren says yes on their own terms: staying means a real life, shared. Beat: resolution of the external plot; the fake becomes official and chosen.

chapters.title: Verity's Small Surrender
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Verity visits alone, admitting she enforced the vow's letter because she, too, once chose safety over love. She concedes the building and, almost, an apology. Beat: the antagonist humanized; the theme of inheritance—what we pass down—made explicit.

chapters.title: Renovations and Revels
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. The shop expands: Wren's bindery opens to the town, Juniper gets a reading nook, and the found family assembles shelves together. Beat: warm denouement; belonging built in wood and paper; Juniper's wish list fulfilled item by item.

chapters.title: Anniversary of the Vow
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. On the tenth anniversary of Sam's death, Gideon visits the grave with Wren and Juniper, thanking Sam and releasing the old vow. Beat: grief honored, not erased; the emotional debt of chapter nine paid in full.

chapters.title: What the Heart Is For
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren reflects in the bindery: the heart is a muscle like any other—trainable, yes, but trained for this, for staying. A new customer enters and is welcomed by all three. Beat: the blurb's thesis answered and overturned; fullness without sentimentality.

chapters.title: When the Vow Burns
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV, closing frame. One year later: the reunion invitation arrives again—next year at Eastwick Books, hosted by Gideon, Wren, and Juniper. Gideon pins it above the register where Odile's portrait now hangs. Final beat: the vow burned down to its truth—love, spoken, kept.
